prompt: The mean of $\{6, 8, 10, 12\}$ is $9$. If you add $4$ to **each** value, what is the new mean?
hint: When every value goes up by the same amount, the whole data set slides along the number line together.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Sort the data from least to greatest first — many statistics get easy after that.
When every value goes up by the same amount, the whole data set slides along the number line together.
Each of the four values rises by $4$, so the fair share rises by $4$ too. Add $4$ to the old mean of $9$.

explanation: Adding $4$ to each of the $4$ values raises the total by $4 \times 4 = 16$, from $36$ to $52$.
The count is still $4$, so the new mean is $52 \div 4 = 13$.
This matches the shortcut that adding the same number to every value shifts the mean by that number: $9 + 4 = 13$.
The new mean of the data set is $13$.
